clue.text: He landed early blows in the fight of the century

definitions.text: He landed early blows in the fight of the century

parts.words: He landed early blows in the fight of the century
parts.note: reads like a boxer winning an early-round bout in a heavyweight 'fight of the century', but the fight is the Hundred Years' War and the man an English commander who won its early battles

explanation.walkthrough: The 'fight of the century' sounds like a boxing match; here it is a war that lasted about a century, and the early blows are the English victories at Crécy and Poitiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward of Woodstock, eldest son of Edward III, led English armies to victory at Crécy and Poitiers in the opening phase of the Hundred Years' War.

clue.text: Index constituent may have this number inside

definitions.text: Index constituent may have this number inside

parts.words: Index constituent may have this number inside
parts.note: a share within a stock-market index carries a proportional share of the total, and the word for that carries a number (eight) written inside it

explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition with a nudge: each company in an index is given a share of the whole, and the word for that share has the number EIGHT sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In an index such as the FTSE 100, each company's influence on the figure is set by its proportional share of the total.

parts.note: recto is the right-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: A vicar delighted to have turned to the correct page of the hymnbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'right!' looks like approval; it is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England, often in charge of a parish whose tithes were his own.

explanation.surface: Where a mobster goes to lie low.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a criminal thug, slang hood; and a hood is a covering that hides something away from view.

parts.note: to break into something is to interrupt it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A stretch of time when everything is smashed up, a break in normal life.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage done by things getting broken, smashed crockery being the usual example.

parts.note: read as 'main stay': a call to stop (stay) used on the main, the sea, by sailors

explanation.walkthrough: A mainstay is normally a key support or a ship's rope; split it into 'main' (the sea) and 'stay' (stop!) and you have a sailor's order to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical command meaning stop or cease, shouted aboard ship.

indicators.note: the phrase for knowing goes round, placed about, the word for desire

parts.note: ken is Scottish and old English for to know
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Wanting to learn all about cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: The cooking room of a house, and by extension the style of cooking a restaurant offers.

clue.text: Soothsayer gives this warning to actors

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A seer tells a theatre company that trouble lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is shouted on a golf course to warn players a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A prediction of what is to come is what a seer offers.

indicators.note: the word for scrubbing has its first letter put out

parts.note: scrubbing is cleaning

explanation.surface: A cleaner's preference is to get the scrubbing done first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out first' removes the C at the front of CLEANING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency or propensity, a slope of the mind toward something.

explanation.surface: Sailors' drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall glass for sherry or beer, and a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigged masts.

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word string is taken

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English executioner whose name came to mean any hangman

explanation.surface: A hangman's noose made from a drawstring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw-string' looks like one word, but it splits into the definition 'Draw' and 'string', whose first letter is S.
explanation.definitionFit: To sketch is to make a quick rough drawing.

clue.text: Fool takes swim in river? Quite the reverse!

indicators.note: the surface puts the swim inside the river
this swaps the roles, so the river goes inside the swim instead

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: A fool going for a dip in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts DIP in R; 'Quite the reverse' tells you to put R in DIP instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a feeble, dull person, a wet.

clue.text: Having missed confession, there's trouble for nun over fig

indicators.note: the letters are put in trouble, thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A nun skipped confession and is in trouble over a fig.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin not confessed has not been absolved, so it remains unpardoned.

clue.text: It is working with several functions

definitions.text: It is working with several functions

indicators.note: the letters are set working, moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gadget that does many jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges IT and SEVERAL, and the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptable that can serve many different uses.

clue.text: Guard against fall when rubella outbreak overwhelms many

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, overwhelm, the letter for many
the word rubella breaks out into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Measures to protect people when a German measles epidemic sweeps through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak' turns RUBELLA into UBRELLA and 'overwhelms' puts M inside it. The fall is rainfall, not a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly shields its holder from falling rain.

indicators.note: the name for a man comes after, follows, the word for a plan

parts.note: a regimen is a planned course of diet or exercise
Ted, short for Edward, stands for any man

explanation.surface: A man told to stick to the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly organised, as a regiment is.

indicators.note: the letters for credit and acceptable go inside the turned word
in a down clue, up means the word for line is read backwards

parts.note: a tier is a row or line
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Collecting acceptable credit in a line-up of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line-up' splits: TIER read upwards is REIT, with CR and U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit is to enlist or round up new members, gathering supporters.

clue.text: Harlot written about in Shakespeare, for instance

indicators.note: the word is turned about, written backwards

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard

explanation.surface: A prostitute who appears in Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A drab is an old word for a slattern or prostitute.

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Making money at the shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle over terms is to negotiate a deal, a sense of trading.

indicators.note: the name of the code inventor takes in the letter for nothing

parts.note: Samuel Morse devised the code named after him
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A codebreaker writes down nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' sits at the end as the definition, in its feeling-low sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullen and gloomy, feeling low.

parts.note: eery, a variant of eerie, means strange and uncanny

explanation.surface: An odd child who is nevertheless cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright and in good spirits.

clue.text: Keen to write up half hearted music

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, reversed
the doubled middle letters lose one of the pair, half the heart

parts.note: reggae is Jamaican popular music

explanation.surface: Eager to review half-hearted music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half hearted' drops one G from the middle GG of REGGAE, giving REGAE; 'to write up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and enthusiastic.

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society girl
a programme being transmitted is on air

explanation.surface: A carefree young woman going on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes someone suave and casually confident.

clue.text: Emperor of island race wears spectacles

indicators.note: the spectacles surround, are worn round, the race

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An island's ruler competes in a race wearing glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto the Great and later Ottos were Holy Roman Emperors.

clue.text: Returning animal you heard near midnight; a cow maybe

indicators.note: the animal's name comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope

indicators.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

parts.note: the pronoun spoken out loud
late in the evening, close to midnight

explanation.surface: A homecoming animal you heard around midnight might be a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns GNU into UNG; YOU sounds like U.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofed mammal; cows, horses and deer are all examples.

clue.text: For temptress love happened in US city

indicators.note: the letters go inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
love is zero in tennis, O
lit, as in 'lit upon', means happened or came across

explanation.surface: Love found by chance in Los Angeles with a seductive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit on' means happened upon, so LIT stands for happened.
explanation.definitionFit: From Nabokov's novel, the name for a sexually precocious girl, a young seductress.

clue.text: Arrange order to a ritual slaughterman

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to set up a ritual killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter kills the bull in the ritual of the corrida.

indicators.note: the word for always is kept inside the symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
ever means always

explanation.surface: A flower that is forever stored in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river; the SEVERN is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, so in crosswords a flower is a river.
